deep.reconstruction:
Overview. The page states three things: (10) the modular invariant (Dedekind's 'Valenz') as a rational function of the modulus; (11) the standard eta-quotient expressions for k, k', K and the four theta-nullwerte, with the remark that a simple derivation 'from the above principles' has not yet been found; and (12) the stated aim of the whole study, a grounded theory of modular ('Valenz') equations and complex multiplication. The page carries the explicit marker '(Dedekind)'. Its content, terminology ('Valenz', val, eta) and section numbering match Dedekind's 1877 letter to Borchardt. It is most likely a draft or excerpt of Dedekind's work kept in the Riemann Nachlass. Throughout, the notation 1^x means e^{2πix} and q = e^{πiω}.

§10. In this formula k denotes Legendre's λ = k_Jacobi² (my reading).
- The claim is v = val(ω) = (4/27)(k+ρ)^3(k+ρ²)^3 / (k²(1−k)²), with ρ = e^{2πi/3}.
- [Mine] Since (k+ρ)(k+ρ²) = k² − k + 1, this is f(ω) = (4/27)(λ²−λ+1)³/(λ²(1−λ)²), i.e. J = j/1728.
- Invariance: f(ω+1) = f(ω). [Mine] More fully, f is unchanged under λ→1−λ, 1/λ, λ/(λ−1), so f is invariant under the full modular group. It is therefore a single-valued function of v.
- Poles: f can be infinite only where λ = 0, 1, ∞. Since λ and 1−λ are eta-quotients (k = θ2⁴/θ3⁴), this happens only at the cusps, i.e. where v = ∞, e.g. ω = i∞.
- Behaviour at the cusp: there λ ~ 16q, so f ~ (4/27)/(256q²) = 1/(1728 e^{2πiω}). Hence f·e^{2πiω} → 2^{-6}3^{-3}, and f/v is finite and nonzero at the cusp.
- Conclusion: f is linear in v (Liouville-type argument on the modular curve), f = a + b·v.
- Normalisation: ω = ρ gives λ = −ρ = e^{−iπ/3}, a root of λ²−λ+1, so f = 0 where v = 0. ω = i gives λ = 1/2, so f = (4/27)(27/64)/(1/16) = 1 where v = 1. Hence f = v.

§11. Now k is the Jacobi modulus, k' its complement, K, K' the usual periods, iK' = Kω, and η(ω) = 1^{ω/24}∏(1−1^{νω}) = q^{1/12}∏(1−q^{2ν}).
- Moduli and period:
  - k^{1/4} = e^{πi/24}√2 η(2ω)/η((1+ω)/2)
  - k'^{1/4} = e^{πi/24} η(ω/2)/η((1+ω)/2), with k² + k'² = 1
  - √(2K/π) = e^{−πi/12} η((1+ω)/2)²/η(ω)
- Theta functions, with period 1 in z:
  - ϑ(z) = Σ (−1)^s q^{s²} e^{2πisz}, i.e. Jacobi's θ0/θ4
  - ϑ1(z) = −Σ e^{2πi[(s+½)²ω/2 + (s+½)(z+½)]}
  - ϑ2(z) = Σ q^{(s+½)²} e^{2πi(s+½)z}
  - ϑ3(z) = Σ q^{s²} e^{2πisz}
- Theta-nullwerte:
  - ϑ(0) = η(ω/2)²/η(ω)
  - ϑ1'(0) = 2π η(ω)³ (the factor 2π because of the period-1 normalisation in z)
  - ϑ2(0) = 2η(2ω)²/η(ω)
  - ϑ3(0) = e^{−πi/12} η((1+ω)/2)²/η(ω)
- [Mine] The k, k', K formulas follow from k = ϑ2²/ϑ3², k' = ϑ²/ϑ3² and 2K/π = ϑ3².
- The author states that a simple derivation of these representations from 'the above principles' (presumably the valence/fundamental-domain theory of earlier sections) has not yet succeeded.

§12. Purpose of the investigation.
- Take integers A, B, C, D with AD − BC = n > 0. Then W = val((C+Dω)/(A+Bω)) is an algebraic function of v = val(ω); this is the modular (transformation) equation of order n.
- This is a special case of the general question: which single-valued functions of ω are algebraic functions of v? Answer (modern): the modular functions for subgroups commensurable with SL2(Z).
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every formula checks against standard q-expansions, including the constants e^{πi/24}, e^{−πi/12} and 2^{-6}3^{-3}.

The §10 argument is sketched. Invariance is stated only for ω→ω+1, but single-valuedness in v needs invariance under the whole modular group. That holds because the expression is symmetric under the anharmonic group acting on λ.
In §10, k means λ = k_Jacobi². In §11, k is the Jacobi modulus (k² + k'² = 1). The same letter is used in two senses.
'K i' = Kω' should read iK' = Kω.

results.what: Modular invariant as rational function of λ: J = val(ω) = 4/27 (λ²−λ+1)³/(λ²(1−λ)²), normalised by J(ρ) = 0 and J(i) = 1; proof via invariance, pole analysis at the cusp and linearity
results.modern_name: Klein's absolute invariant J = j/1728 expressed in Legendre λ (Dedekind's 'Valenz')

results.what: Eta-quotient expressions for k^{1/4}, k'^{1/4}, √(2K/π) and the four theta-nullwerte, including ϑ1' = 2πη³
results.modern_name: Eta-product formulas for theta constants (Jacobi triple product identities)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova, 1829), written in eta notation by Dedekind (1877)
Dedekind (1877, Erläuterungen zu Riemanns Fragmenten / Borchardt letter)

results.what: val((C+Dω)/(A+Bω)) is algebraic over val(ω) for an integer matrix of determinant n; general question of which single-valued functions of ω are algebraic in J
results.modern_name: Modular equation for j / modular functions for congruence (commensurable) subgroups
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi, Kronecker, Hermite (modular equations); Dedekind 1877 and Klein for the J-function formulation

deep.surprise_reason: The page is explicitly marked '(Dedekind)'. Its numbering, terminology ('Valenz', val, η) and closing programme coincide with Dedekind's 1877 letter to Borchardt, so it is almost certainly Dedekind's work (draft or copy) preserved in the Riemann Nachlass, not new Riemann material. If it were genuinely Riemann's, an early use of the eta function and the J-as-valence theory would be notable. The attribution evidence, however, points firmly to Dedekind, whose authorship of this material is well known.

'K i' = Kω' should be 'K'i = Kω' (iK' = Kω).
'und nun nenn [?]' is likely 'und wenn man' (… setzt, so ist).
'nur dann, wenn v = ∞, also z. B. ω = ∞ wird' is plausible as transcribed.
'Nun kann setzen' should probably read 'Man kann setzen'.
'(Dedekind)' after 'nicht gelungen' is an explicit attribution marker. The page appears to be Dedekind's text (cf. his 1877 Borchardt letter), not Riemann's.
